speaker: Doctor
text:
The ECG and metabolic panel results are normal, so we need to look elsewhere. Did you experience any warning symptoms like palpitations, chest pain, or visual changes just before you lost consciousness?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count
REQUEST TEST: Toxicology Screen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Within normal limits. Toxicology Screen: Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The CBC and toxicology screen are normal, which helps rule out infection and drug-induced causes. To further evaluate the risk of a cardiac arrhythmia or seizure, did you notice any rhythmic jerking movements or tongue biting during the episode?

REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI
REQUEST IMAGES: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Brain MRI: No abnormalities. EEG: Within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI and EEG are both normal, which effectively rules out seizure activity and structural brain issues. I need to determine if this was a vasovagal episode or related to orthostatic hypotension: did you feel lightheaded or dizzy immediately before the loss of consciousness, and were you standing up at the time it happened?

REQUEST TEST: Orthostatic Vitals
REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Orthostatic Vitals: No significant change in blood pressure or heart rate upon standing. Echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular size and function, no wall motion abnormalities, no valvular pathology.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal orthostatic vitals and echocardiogram rule out structural heart disease and significant orthostatic hypotension. Since we have excluded cardiac, metabolic, toxicological, and epileptic causes, did you experience any palpitations, chest discomfort, or shortness of breath prior to the episode?

REQUEST TEST: Carotid Doppler
REQUEST TEST: Head CT (non-contrast)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Carotid Doppler: No significant stenosis or dissection. Head CT (non-contrast): No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or ischemic changes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The carotid doppler and head CT are normal, ruling out stroke and significant vascular issues. Since we have exhausted cardiac, metabolic, and neurological causes, have you been under extreme physical stress, emotional distress, or have you had a bowel movement immediately before the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of syncope occurring immediately after urination is highly suggestive of micturition syncope. Given the negative cardiac, neurological, and metabolic workup so far, do you have any history of heart disease, diabetes, or a family history of sudden cardiac death?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope
